title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation fraud carried out with synthetic media. A caller used a deepfake video and voice to present himself as a sitting chief minister on a live WhatsApp video call, and the victim treated that presentation as sufficient proof of identity. The same operation then added a second impersonation, of a CBI officer, to escalate the demands. The failure sits at the point of contact between a member of the public and a communication channel that carries no verification of who is on the other end.

Nothing in the deployment prevented the call from being made or received. Catching it would have required the victim to have an independent way to confirm that the person on the call was the official he claimed to be, since the audio and video themselves were the only evidence offered. The fraud also depended on a payment flow in which fees, exchange charges, unlock charges and fines were requested and paid through a digital payment app without any check on the recipient.

What is not established is who made the deepfake or operated the scheme, and the registration of a case under the Information Technology Act is not a finding of guilt against any person.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using a deepfake video and voice to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. The manager then demanded fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh through a digital payment app after another person posing as a CBI officer demanded more money as a fine. He stopped when the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000. He reported the case to the cybercrime helpline and Byappanahalli police, and a case has been registered under the Information Technology Act.
